topics.title: 高级语法:倒装与分裂句
topics.description: 用于强调的结构性工具

guide.intro: 在 C1 阶段,用不同的结构传达相同信息是制造重音的关键手段。倒装(inversion)、分裂句(cleft sentences)和前置(fronting)都是 C1 的标志性手法。

sections.text: 否定倒装
当否定或限制性副词位于句首时,主语与助动词需要调换位置:「Rarely have I seen such talent」、「Not only did he refuse, he also walked out」。
分裂句
It-分裂句(It is X who/that…)与 What-分裂句(What I need is…)用于突出特定成分:「It was John who broke the vase」(打碎花瓶的是 John),「What I want is silence」(我想要的是安静)。

rows.source: It was Sarah who first noticed the error.
rows.translation: 最先注意到这一错误的人是 Sarah。

rows.source: What surprises me most is his silence.
rows.translation: 最让我惊讶的是他的沉默。

rows.source: Rarely have we encountered such resistance.
rows.translation: 我们很少遇到这样的抗拒。

rows.source: Not only is the policy ineffective, it is also costly.
rows.translation: 该政策不仅无效,而且代价高昂。

sections.text: 倒装多用于正式写作和演说;在日常对话中显得做作。你会在学术文章和新闻文本里经常见到。

lessons.title: 否定倒装
lessons.description: 句首的否定副词

exercises.prompt: 「我这辈子很少见过这样的才华」用正式的倒装句怎么表达?
options: I have rarely seen such talent in my life.
Rarely have I seen such talent in my life.
Rarely I have seen such talent in my life.
Rarely seen I such talent in my life.
exercises.answer: Rarely have I seen such talent in my life.

exercises.prompt: Never before ___ I felt such pressure.
exercises.answer: had
exercises.hint: 我以前从未感受过这么大的压力。

exercises.prompt: 「他不仅拒绝,还离开了房间。」
exercises.answer: Not only did he refuse but he also walked out

exercises.prompt: 开头 — 含义
下列哪一句是正确的倒装句?
options: Hardly I had arrived when the storm broke.
Hardly had I arrived when the storm broke.
Hardly had I arrive when the storm broke.
Hardly I arrived when the storm broke.
exercises.answer: Hardly had I arrived when the storm broke.

exercises.prompt: 出你听到的句子
exercises.spokenText: Under no circumstances should you reveal the source.
options: Under no circumstances should you reveal the source.
Under no circumstance should you reveal the source.
Under no circumstances should you revealed the source.
Under no circumstances you should reveal the source.
exercises.answer: Under no circumstances should you reveal the source.

exercises.prompt: No sooner ___ I sat down than the phone rang.
exercises.answer: had
exercises.hint: 我刚坐下，电话就响了。

exercises.prompt: 倒装属于哪种语域?
exercises.answer: 正式 / 文学
exercises.explanation: 倒装句多见于学术写作、新闻评论、正式演说;若用于日常对话会显得做作。

exercises.prompt: 「在任何情况下都不应让门保持敞开。」
exercises.answer: Under no circumstances should the door be left open

exercises.prompt: Little ___ they realise the danger.
exercises.answer: did
exercises.explanation: 「Little did they realise」 是惯用的倒装表达。
exercises.hint: 他们几乎没有意识到危险。

lessons.title: 分裂句
lessons.description: It-分裂句与 What-分裂句

exercises.prompt: 「最先注意到错误的是 Sarah」 用英语怎么说?
options: It was Sarah who first noticed the error.
exercises.answer: It was Sarah who first noticed the error.

exercises.prompt: ___ surprises me most is his silence.
exercises.answer: What
exercises.hint: 最让我吃惊的就是他的沉默。

exercises.prompt: 「我真正需要的是时间。」
exercises.answer: What I really need is time

exercises.prompt: 分裂句结构 — 强调重心
「It was in 2008 that the crisis hit」 用中文怎么翻译?
options: 正是在 2008 年危机才爆发。
exercises.answer: 正是在 2008 年危机才爆发。
exercises.explanation: It-cleft 把重音放在时间上,对应中文「正是 / 就是……才……」的「是……的」结构。

exercises.prompt: 出你听到的句子
exercises.spokenText: What concerns me most is the lack of transparency.
options: What concerns me most is the lack of transparency.
What concern me most is the lack of transparency.
What concerns me most is the lacks of transparency.
What concerns me most is the lack of transparencies.
exercises.answer: What concerns me most is the lack of transparency.

exercises.prompt: It is the patient ___ deserves our attention.
exercises.answer: who
exercises.hint: 需要我们关注的正是病人本身。

exercises.prompt: 「All I want is honesty」 用中文怎么说?
options: 我唯一想要的就是诚实。
exercises.answer: 我唯一想要的就是诚实。
exercises.explanation: 「All + 主语 + 动词 + is X」 = 「我所……的只是 X」;伪分裂句结构,强调「唯一」。

exercises.prompt: 「做出决定的是委员会,而不是某个个人。」
exercises.answer: It was the committee that made the decision not an individual

exercises.prompt: It was ___ here that we first met.
exercises.answer: right
exercises.hint: 我们当初就是在这里第一次见面的。

lessons.title: 分词从句
lessons.description: 用 -ing 和 -ed 构成的简短分句

exercises.prompt: 「她结束会议后离开了办公室」 用分词结构应该怎么写?
options: Finishing the meeting, she left the office.
Having finished the meeting, she left the office.
She finished meeting and left office.
exercises.answer: Having finished the meeting, she left the office.

exercises.prompt: ___ in haste, the report contained errors.
exercises.answer: Written
exercises.hint: 由于报告写得仓促，里面出现了错误。

exercises.prompt: 「她因为感到疲倦,早早就上床睡觉了。」
exercises.answer: Feeling tired she went to bed early

exercises.prompt: 结构 — 含义
「Approved by the board, the plan went ahead」 用中文怎么说?
options: 因被董事会批准,该方案得以推进。
exercises.answer: 因被董事会批准,该方案得以推进。
exercises.explanation: 「Approved by X, NP did Y」 是被动分词作状语;中文 L1 容易把这种简化关系从句当作完整主句来译,导致语义错乱。

exercises.prompt: 出你听到的句子
exercises.spokenText: Having reviewed the data, she drew her conclusions.
options: Having reviewed the data, she drew her conclusions.
Having review the data, she drew her conclusions.
Have reviewed the data, she drew her conclusions.
Having reviewed the data, she draw her conclusions.
exercises.answer: Having reviewed the data, she drew her conclusions.

exercises.prompt: ___ at the airport, we headed to the hotel.
exercises.answer: Having arrived
exercises.hint: 我们到了机场之后就直接去了酒店。

exercises.prompt: 下列哪个分词结构是错误的?
options: Walking down the street, I saw an old friend.
Walked down the street, I saw an old friend.
Having walked down the street, I saw an old friend.
Being tired, I went to bed early.
exercises.answer: Walked down the street, I saw an old friend.
exercises.explanation: 表达主动含义时需用 「-ing」。

exercises.prompt: 「这一被董事会审阅过的方案已获批准。」
exercises.answer: Reviewed by the board the plan was approved

exercises.prompt: ___ ignored, the problem grew worse.
exercises.answer: Being
exercises.hint: 由于一直被忽视，这个问题越来越严重。

lessons.title: 分裂句与前置
lessons.description: 有意识地放置重音

exercises.prompt: 「It was the price that worried us」 是一个 ___ 句子。
exercises.answer: it-cleft
exercises.explanation: 「It is/was X that…」 即为 it-分裂句结构。

exercises.prompt: ___ I really want is a clear timeline.
exercises.answer: What
exercises.explanation: Wh-分裂句:「What I want is X.」
exercises.hint: 我真正想要的是一个明确的时间表。

exercises.prompt: 结构 — 例句

pairs.right: It was John who solved it.
What we need is more time.
Never have I seen such a thing.
It is essential that he attend.

exercises.prompt: 「我们真正需要的是一份更清晰的简报。」
exercises.answer: What we really need is a clearer brief

exercises.prompt: 「Never have I encountered such resistance」 属于什么结构?
exercises.answer: 否定前置 + 倒装
exercises.explanation: 当否定副词(never/rarely/seldom/hardly)位于句首时,主谓需倒装(助动词在主语前)。中文 L1 易遗漏这种助动词倒装。

exercises.prompt: 出你听到的句子
exercises.spokenText: Not until the audit was completed did we grasp the full picture.
options: Not until the audit was completed did we grasp the full picture.
Not until the audit was completed we grasped the full picture.
Not until the audit was completed did we grasped the full picture.
Not until the audits were completed do we grasp the full picture.
exercises.answer: Not until the audit was completed did we grasp the full picture.

exercises.prompt: It ___ not until 2020 that we noticed the trend.
exercises.answer: was
exercises.hint: 直到二零二零年我们才注意到这一趋势。

exercises.prompt: 下列哪一句是正确的前置(fronting)示例?
options: Rarely have we seen such growth.
Rarely we have seen such growth.
We rarely have seen such growth, however.
Have rarely we seen such growth.
exercises.answer: Rarely have we seen such growth.

exercises.prompt: 「真正让我感到困扰的是透明度的缺乏。」
exercises.answer: What really troubled me was the lack of transparency

exercises.prompt: Only ___ examining the data did we identify the bias.
exercises.answer: after
exercises.explanation: 即 「Only after V-ing… did we…」 的结构。
exercises.hint: 只有在分析数据之后，我们才发现这种偏差。

exercises.prompt: 「It was X who first raised the issue」 这一分裂句结构强调的是什么?
exercises.answer: 强调 Sarah(谁做的)
exercises.explanation: It-cleft 把焦点放在 「Sarah」 上;对应中文「是 Sarah 第一个提出这个问题的」(「是……的」 强调焦点)。

exercises.prompt: 「在任何情况下我们都不会重回原协议。」
exercises.answer: Under no circumstances will we revert to the agreement

lessons.title: 高级关系从句与分词结构
lessons.description: 简化关系从句、分词从句、非限定结构

exercises.prompt: 「The report submitted yesterday is incomplete.」 属于什么结构?
exercises.answer: Reduced passive relative ('which was submitted')
exercises.explanation: 「which was submitted」 可简化为 「submitted」(过去分词短语)。

exercises.prompt: The candidate ___ for the role has fifteen years of experience.
exercises.answer: selected
exercises.hint: 被选中担任这一职位的候选人有十五年的工作经验。

exercises.prompt: 结构 — 定义

pairs.right: 不可省略,省略后含义改变;不加逗号

exercises.prompt: 「主导谈判的顾问今天将做汇报。」
exercises.answer: The consultant leading the negotiation will report today

exercises.prompt: 在 「The findings, which were unexpected, prompted further study」 中,为什么要加逗号?
options: 因为这是非限定(补充信息)的从句
exercises.answer: 因为这是非限定(补充信息)的从句
exercises.explanation: 中文里不区分限定/非限定从句,因此中文 L1 学习者常常漏掉逗号;在英语中,逗号差异会改变语义。

exercises.prompt: 出你听到的句子
exercises.spokenText: Having reviewed the proposal, we are prepared to move forward.
options: Having reviewed the proposal, we are prepared to move forward.
Having review the proposal, we are prepared to move forward.
Having reviewed the proposals, we is prepared to move forward.
Have reviewed the proposal, we are prepared to move forward.
exercises.answer: Having reviewed the proposal, we are prepared to move forward.

exercises.prompt: ___ all things considered, the deal is fair.
exercises.answer: All
exercises.explanation: 独立分词结构:「all things considered」。
exercises.hint: 综合各方面来看，这笔交易是公平的。

exercises.prompt: 下列哪一句正确使用了分词从句?
options: Walking to work, my phone rang.
Walking to work, I noticed the new café.
Walking to work, the new café opened.
While walking to work, the new café was visible.
exercises.answer: Walking to work, I noticed the new café.
exercises.explanation: 分词的逻辑主语必须与主句一致:走路的是「I」,不是手机。

exercises.prompt: 「考虑到所做的分析,这一结论是站得住脚的。」
exercises.answer: Given the analysis conducted the conclusion is defensible

exercises.prompt: The author, ___ work has shaped the field, will keynote.
exercises.answer: whose
exercises.hint: 这位作品塑造了这一领域的作家将担任主讲。

exercises.prompt: 「Rules permitting, we'll launch on Friday」 属于什么结构?
options: 简化的 'if' 条件句(独立分词结构)
exercises.answer: 简化的 'if' 条件句(独立分词结构)
exercises.explanation: 「If rules permit」 = 「rules permitting」(独立主格);中文「如规则允许」对应。注意主语和分词必须搭配。

exercises.prompt: 很荣幸认识你。
exercises.answer: Weather permitting the opening will take place tomorrow

lessons.title: 对话:与编辑就稿件展开拉锯
lessons.description: 通过分裂句与倒装句转移重音

exercises.prompt: 编辑驳回稿件

turns.speaker: editor
turns.text: Your lede buries the actual story. The reader shouldn't have to wait three paragraphs to find out who did what to whom.

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: 为自己的写作辩护 — 用分裂句提出方案
options: Sure thing, I'll just put the answer in like the first sentence then.
What I was trying to foreground was the institutional context, not the individual actor — but I take your point and I'll restructure.
I don't get why you don't like it, it reads fine to me.
turns.answer: What I was trying to foreground was the institutional context, not the individual actor — but I take your point and I'll restructure.

turns.speaker: editor
turns.text: Foregrounding context is fine, but your verbs are limp. Half this draft is in passive voice.

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: 倒装强调 — 请补全助动词
turns.after: I revise the verbs, I'll also tighten the modifiers — the draft has accreted some lazy hedges.
turns.answer: will

turns.speaker: editor
turns.text: Good. And the kicker? It lands like a wet sponge. We need a closing line that actually closes.

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: 分裂句 + 建议 — 请选择自然的写作语言
options: It is precisely the absence of a verdict in the source material that I was trying to mirror — but I can sharpen the ambiguity into something more deliberate.
Yeah the ending sucks, my bad, I'll fix it.
Honestly endings are hard, can you just write it for me?
turns.answer: It is precisely the absence of a verdict in the source material that I was trying to mirror — but I can sharpen the ambiguity into something more deliberate.

turns.speaker: editor
turns.text: Sharpened ambiguity, I can work with. But the pull-quote needs an attribution; it's currently floating.

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: 分词结构 — 请填入正确的形式
turns.after: the source on background, I had to scrub the attribution — but I can negotiate a partial reveal with her press team.
turns.answer: Having interviewed

turns.speaker: editor
turns.text: Negotiate hard. A floating quote in a piece this length will be picked apart on social.

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: 在书面话语中以 C1 水准收尾
options: Sure thing, I'll just text her or whatever.
Understood — I'll push for at least an on-the-record paraphrase and route the revision past you before filing.
turns.answer: Understood — I'll push for at least an on-the-record paraphrase and route the revision past you before filing.

turns.speaker: editor
turns.text: By Thursday, please. We're holding the slot but I won't hold it indefinitely.

turns.speaker: you
turns.text: Thursday it is. I'll send the revised draft and a note flagging every change I've made.

topics.title: 辩论与演说
topics.description: 正式辩论中的话语语言

guide.intro: 正式辩论(debate)遵循特定结构:opening(开篇)、rebuttal(反驳)、summary(总结)。词汇选择反映出说话者的信念与逻辑。C1 阶段的说话者会将流利度与词汇的多样性结合起来。

sections.text: 辩论功能

rows: I'd like to begin by addressing…
With respect, I must take issue with…
The argument falls apart when we consider…
In conclusion, the case is clear: …

sections.text: 演说性形容词
演说中的形容词选择决定语气。「Profound」 = 深刻;「compelling」 = 极具说服力;「tenuous」 = 脆弱、勉强;「specious」 = 看似合理实则站不住脚;「unfounded」 = 毫无根据。

rows.source: The argument is compelling, but ultimately flawed.
rows.translation: 论证颇具说服力,但最终仍存在缺陷。

rows.source: These claims are wholly unfounded.
rows.translation: 这些指控完全没有依据。

rows.source: The reasoning, while seductive, is specious.
rows.translation: 论证看似诱人,实则似是而非。

sections.text: 在英语辩论中,「with respect」 实际上是用来软化反对的措辞。其作用相当于中文里的「恕我直言」或「请允许我冒昧地说」。

lessons.title: 主张与反主张
lessons.description: 熟记句子的开头模式

exercises.prompt: 功能 — 句式

pairs.right: I'd like to begin by addressing…
With respect, I must take issue with…
The argument falls apart when we consider…

exercises.prompt: 「It is my contention that…」 用中文怎么说?
exercises.answer: 我的主张是……
exercises.explanation: 「contention」 是「主张 / 论点」(辩论专用);中文 L1 易因「contend」与「contest」相近而混淆。

exercises.prompt: With ___, I must disagree.
exercises.answer: respect
exercises.hint: 恕我直言，我不能同意。

exercises.prompt: 「在更深入审视后,这一论证便站不住脚了。」
exercises.answer: The argument falls apart on closer inspection

exercises.prompt: 下列哪个形容词用于描述「极具说服力的论证」?
exercises.answer: compelling

exercises.prompt: 出你听到的句子
exercises.spokenText: These claims are wholly unfounded.
exercises.answer: These claims are wholly unfounded.

exercises.prompt: The reasoning is ___; it merely appears valid.
exercises.answer: specious
exercises.hint: 这种论证看似合理，实则站不住脚。

exercises.prompt: 「tenuous」 用中文怎么说?
exercises.answer: 薄弱、勉强
exercises.explanation: 「tenuous link / claim」 = 「勉强的关联 / 站不住脚的主张」;辩论中用以批评对方论证。

exercises.prompt: 「总而言之,该主张是站不住脚的。」
exercises.answer: In conclusion the case fails

exercises.prompt: I would ___ urge you to reconsider.
exercises.answer: respectfully
exercises.hint: 我想恭敬地请您重新考虑。

lessons.title: 演说性形容词及其细微差别
lessons.description: 为论证语气挑选词汇

exercises.prompt: 形容词 — 中文释义
「profound」 是什么意思?
exercises.answer: 深刻 / 意味深长
exercises.explanation: 「profound」 ≠ 「professional」;中文 L1 易将词形相近的两词混淆。「profound」 = 「深远的、深刻的」。

exercises.prompt: The implications are ___
exercises.answer: profound
exercises.hint: 这其中的影响极为深远。

exercises.prompt: 「这个论证看似诱人,实则毫无根据。」
exercises.answer: The argument is seductive but unfounded

exercises.prompt: 哪个形容词承载着「看似有说服力但实则错误」的语气?
exercises.answer: specious

exercises.prompt: 出你听到的句子
exercises.spokenText: The link between these variables is tenuous at best.
options: The link between these variables is tenuous at best.
The link between these variable is tenuous at best.
The link between these variables is tenuous at beast.
The link between these variables are tenuous at best.
exercises.answer: The link between these variables is tenuous at best.

exercises.prompt: These accusations are ___
exercises.answer: unfounded
exercises.hint: 这些指控毫无根据。

exercises.prompt: 「rigorous」 用中文怎么说?
exercises.answer: 严谨 / 缜密
exercises.explanation: 「rigorous analysis / methodology」 = 「严谨的分析 / 方法」;辩论中称赞对方时常用。

exercises.prompt: 「这不是严谨的分析,只是空泛的揣测。」
exercises.answer: This is not rigorous analysis but mere speculation

exercises.prompt: Their reasoning is ___ flawed.
exercises.answer: fundamentally
exercises.hint: 他们的论证存在根本性的缺陷。

lessons.title: 话语标记
lessons.description: Granted、conversely、notwithstanding

exercises.prompt: 话语标记词 — 中文释义
「notwithstanding」 是什么意思?
exercises.answer: 尽管如此 / 不顾……
exercises.explanation: 正式语域中的让步连词;可放句首、句中或句尾(罕见);中文「尽管 / 不论」是常见对应。

exercises.prompt: ___ his concerns, the project went ahead.
exercises.answer: Notwithstanding
exercises.hint: 尽管他有所顾虑，项目还是推进了。

exercises.prompt: 「诚然,这个想法很诱人,然而它并不可行。」
exercises.answer: Granted the idea is appealing however it is not feasible

exercises.prompt: 「Hence」 的语气如何?
options: 正式 / 文言味的「因此」
exercises.answer: 正式 / 文言味的「因此」
exercises.explanation: 「hence」 略带文言色彩,比 「therefore」 更紧凑,比 「so」 更正式;中文「故 / 因而」对应。

exercises.prompt: 出你听到的句子
exercises.spokenText: Conversely, smaller firms reported gains.
exercises.answer: Conversely, smaller firms reported gains.

exercises.prompt: The market has shifted; ___, our strategy must adapt.
exercises.answer: hence
exercises.hint: 市场已经发生变化，因此我们的策略也必须调整。

exercises.prompt: 下列哪个话语标记起到「让步」的作用?
exercises.answer: Granted,

exercises.prompt: 「相反,在小规模分析中呈现出不同的趋势。」
exercises.answer: Conversely the smaller scale analysis shows a different trend

exercises.prompt: ___ the criticism, the policy stands.
exercises.answer: Despite
exercises.hint: 尽管受到批评，这项政策依然有效。

lessons.title: 反驳模式(rebuttal)
lessons.description: 公平地复述对方论点,然后将其击倒

exercises.prompt: 下列哪一句是公平的「反驳」(rebuttal)的开头?
options: If I understand the argument correctly, …
exercises.answer: If I understand the argument correctly, …

exercises.prompt: The argument ___ on a questionable assumption.
exercises.answer: rests
exercises.explanation: 「rest on / hinge on」 = 依赖于……。
exercises.hint: 这一论点建立在一个有问题的假设之上。

exercises.prompt: 反驳策略 — 功能

pairs.right: 指出对方混淆了两个不同概念

pairs.left: The evidence cuts the other way

exercises.prompt: 「该论证将结构性原因与个人选择混为一谈。」
exercises.answer: The argument conflates structural causes with individual choices

exercises.prompt: 「That argument proves too much」 是什么意思?
options: 若接受这一论证,会顺带推出过多荒谬结论,因而有问题
这个论证需要写很多页
exercises.answer: 若接受这一论证,会顺带推出过多荒谬结论,因而有问题
exercises.explanation: 辩论术语:「proves too much」 是逻辑反驳手法 —— 同一论证的逻辑若适用过广,反而暴露其荒谬。

exercises.prompt: 出你听到的句子
exercises.spokenText: Even granting the premise, the conclusion does not follow.
options: Even granting the premise, the conclusion does not follow.
Even granted the premise, the conclusion does not follow.
Even granting the premises, the conclusion do not follow.
Even granting the premise, the conclusions does not follow.
exercises.answer: Even granting the premise, the conclusion does not follow.

exercises.prompt: The conclusion does not ___ from the evidence presented.
exercises.answer: follow
exercises.hint: 结论无法从所给出的证据中得出。

exercises.prompt: 下列哪一句揭示了对方在使用「稻草人谬误」?
exercises.answer: That mischaracterises my position.
exercises.explanation: 「mischaracterise」 = 误述、扭曲;典型的「稻草人」反击。

exercises.prompt: 「这一论证将相关性与因果性混为一谈。」
exercises.answer: This argument confuses correlation with causation

exercises.prompt: The data, ___ properly examined, suggest the opposite.
exercises.answer: when
exercises.explanation: 简化的分词结构:「when properly examined」。
exercises.hint: 如果认真分析，这些数据指向的恰恰是相反的结论。

exercises.prompt: 「You're attacking a position I never held」 用中文应怎样表达?
options: 您在攻击一个我从未持有的立场(即「稻草人谬误」)
您在攻击我以前的立场
exercises.answer: 您在攻击一个我从未持有的立场(即「稻草人谬误」)
exercises.explanation: 「稻草人谬误」 = straw man fallacy:对手歪曲你的立场再加以攻击。这是 C1 辩论中应识别的常见逻辑陷阱。

exercises.prompt: 「一旦其所依赖的假设被推翻,这一论证就会瓦解。」
exercises.answer: The argument collapses once its underlying assumption is rejected

exercises.prompt: 出你听到的句子
exercises.spokenText: She told him that he had misunderstood her position entirely.
options: She told him that he had misunderstood her position entirely.
He told her that she had misunderstood his position entirely.
She told him that she had misunderstood his position entirely.
He told him that he had misunderstood her position entirely.
exercises.answer: She told him that he had misunderstood her position entirely.
exercises.explanation: 中文「他」和「她」 同音(tā),中文 L1 在听英语 「he/she/him/her」 时极易混淆。这条题专门训练你保持指代对象一致。

lessons.title: 让一步再反击
lessons.description: Concede-and-pivot:我同意,但是…

exercises.prompt: 下列哪一句是「让步后转向」(concede-and-pivot)的策略?
options: Granted, the cost is real; that said, the benefits outweigh it.
exercises.answer: Granted, the cost is real; that said, the benefits outweigh it.

exercises.prompt: There is ___ truth to that, but it overlooks the bigger picture.
exercises.answer: some
exercises.hint: 这话有一定道理，但忽略了大局。

exercises.prompt: 话语策略 — 标签

pairs.left: That's true as far as it goes, but…

exercises.prompt: 「你在成本问题上是对的,但不作为的代价更高。」
exercises.answer: You are right about the cost yet inaction is more expensive still

exercises.prompt: 「That's true as far as it goes」 是什么意思?
options: 在一定程度上是对的(但不完整)
exercises.answer: 在一定程度上是对的(但不完整)
exercises.explanation: 「as far as it goes」 = 「就其本身而言」(但有边界);常用于做有限让步后再拓展批评。

exercises.prompt: 出你听到的句子
exercises.spokenText: I take your point about timing; the underlying logic, however, still holds.
options: I take your point about timing; the underlying logic, however, still holds.
I take your point about timing; the underlying logic, however, still hold.
I take your points about timing; the underlying logic, however, still holds.
I take your point about timings; the underlying logics, however, still holds.
exercises.answer: I take your point about timing; the underlying logic, however, still holds.

exercises.prompt: I ___ your concern, but the data still favour the proposal.
exercises.answer: appreciate
exercises.explanation: 「appreciate one's concern」 是礼貌承认对方关切的固定说法。
exercises.hint: 我理解你的顾虑，但数据仍然支持这一提案。

exercises.prompt: 「Be that as it may」 这一表达的功能是什么?
options: 先让一步,再表达不同意见
exercises.answer: 先让一步,再表达不同意见
exercises.explanation: 倒装让步句的化石用法;中文「即便如此 / 话虽如此」对应。属于 C1 / C2 正式语域。

exercises.prompt: 「这一批评是中肯的,但所提出的解决方案仍显不足。」
exercises.answer: The criticism is fair yet the proposed solution falls short

exercises.prompt: Be that ___ it may, the policy remains the most defensible option.
exercises.answer: as
exercises.hint: 尽管如此，这项政策仍然是最经得起推敲的方案。

exercises.prompt: 下列哪一句最自然地体现了「让步后反驳」?
options: Fair enough on the data quality, but the trend is unmistakable.
exercises.answer: Fair enough on the data quality, but the trend is unmistakable.

exercises.prompt: 「即便我接受这一点,结论依然不变。」
exercises.answer: While I concede that point the conclusion still does not change

lessons.title: 对话:学术会议小组中的正式反驳
lessons.description: 让步再反击 — 正式小组讨论中的语言

exercises.prompt: 在小组讨论中回应反方论证

turns.speaker: mod
turns.text: Dr. Yıldız, your opponent argues that your framework collapses under scrutiny. Your rebuttal, please.

turns.speaker: opp
turns.text: The framework presumes rational actors, which empirical work has dismantled for at least two decades.

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: 先让步,再反驳 — C1 演说句式
options: Nope, you're wrong, end of story.
I'd grant the premise on rationality — but the framework was never wedded to it; it survives the move to bounded rationality, as I argue in Chapter 3.
Actually empirical work doesn't even matter that much honestly.
turns.answer: I'd grant the premise on rationality — but the framework was never wedded to it; it survives the move to bounded rationality, as I argue in Chapter 3.

turns.speaker: opp
turns.text: That move, however, hollows out the predictive content. You're left with a model that explains everything and forbids nothing.

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: 倒装强调 — 请补全助动词
turns.after: devoid of forbidden states, the critique would stick — but it generates testable restrictions on transition probabilities, which I document.
turns.answer: indeed

turns.speaker: opp
turns.text: Documenting restrictions is not the same as them surviving falsification. Have any been rejected?

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: 在正式话语中选择 「fair point」 类的表达
options: Fair challenge — and yes, two of the original restrictions failed under the 2022 dataset, which I treat at length in the revised edition.
Don't think so but it's whatever.
turns.answer: Fair challenge — and yes, two of the original restrictions failed under the 2022 dataset, which I treat at length in the revised edition.

turns.speaker: opp
turns.text: Two failures out of how many? At some point one has to ask whether the framework is being protected by ad hoc patches.

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: 正式的让步标记 — 请在空格中填入合适的表达
turns.after: the charge of ad-hocness is one I take seriously — which is precisely why each amendment is tied to a pre-registered prediction, not a post-hoc rescue.
turns.answer: Granted

turns.speaker: mod
turns.text: We have time for a final exchange. Dr. Yıldız, your closing thirty seconds.

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: C1 收尾 — 礼貌但清晰地占据优势
options: The disagreement is real, but it's a disagreement about degree, not about kind — and on that narrower terrain I am happy to leave the verdict to the empirical record.
turns.answer: The disagreement is real, but it's a disagreement about degree, not about kind — and on that narrower terrain I am happy to leave the verdict to the empirical record.

turns.speaker: mod
turns.text: Thank you both. We'll open it to the floor after a short break.

topics.title: 艺术与评论
topics.description: 电影、文学、音乐与画廊文章中的评论英语

guide.intro: 艺术评论英语是一种需要精细把握的语域。人们用 「accomplished」、「derivative」、「evocative」、「heavy-handed」 这类形容词来取代 「good」、「bad」。中文里的「经典」「悲剧」「讽刺」与英文同源词看似对应,但语义范围更窄:「a classic film」 = 某类型的代表作;「tragedy」 是文学体裁;「ironic」 是与预期相反(中文里常被错用为「巧合」)。

sections.text: 评论性形容词
在 C1 阶段的评论写作中,直接说「好」或「坏」显得乏力。「Accomplished」(精湛)和 「masterful」(炉火纯青)用于褒奖;「derivative」(模仿性强)、「contrived」(刻意)、「pretentious」(故作姿态)、「heavy-handed」(粗笨)则用于批评。
习语化的评论句式

rows.source: The film struck a chord with audiences worldwide.
rows.translation: 这部电影触动了全球观众的心弦。

rows.source: The novel falls flat in its final act.
rows.translation: 小说在最后一幕里失去了张力。

rows.source: It is a tour de force of contemporary cinema.
rows.translation: 是当代电影中的一部杰作。

rows.source: A slow burn that rewards patient viewers.
rows.translation: 是一部慢热但回报耐心观众的作品。

rows.source: The album was ahead of its time.
rows.translation: 这张专辑超越了它所处的时代。

rows.source: It's a guilty pleasure of mine.
rows.translation: 是我难以承认却确实喜欢的「秘密快乐」。

sections.text: 中文里的「艺术」涵盖手工艺;但英文 「art」 范围更窄,通常与高雅文化挂钩。表示手工艺时请用 「crafts」 或 「craftsmanship」。
中文里「经典的」有时也带有「典型的/老套的」之意(例如「典型错误」)。但英文 「a classic」 仅指「某类别中的杰出范例」;「典型错误」 = 「a textbook mistake」。

lessons.title: 评论性形容词
lessons.description: 褒义与贬义形容词的细微差别

exercises.prompt: 「成熟而精湛的表演」最适合用哪个形容词?
exercises.answer: accomplished

exercises.prompt: 若要把一部电影评价为「缺乏原创、纯粹模仿」,该用哪个形容词?
exercises.answer: derivative
exercises.explanation: 「derivative」 = 衍生自他人作品、缺乏原创性的。

exercises.prompt: The director's restraint makes the climax all the more ___.
exercises.answer: evocative
exercises.hint: 导演的克制让高潮更加令人回味。

exercises.prompt: 形容词 — 中文对应释义
「Heavy-handed」 这一批评强调的是什么?
exercises.answer: 粗笨、缺少细腻处理
exercises.explanation: 「heavy-handed」 = 「下手过重 / 粗糙」;评论中常用于剧本、配乐过于直白时。中文「拳重」「粗笨」是常见对应。

topics.title: 新闻与评论专栏
topics.description: 新闻、分析与评论专栏语域中的高级英语

guide.intro: 新闻英语包含三种不同的语域:纯报道(reporting)、分析(analysis)与评论专栏(editorial / op-ed)。中文里的「新闻语言」看起来像是一种统一的范式,但在英语中,即便最微小的语气变化 —— 用 「claimed」 替换 「said」、用 「alleged」 替换 「reported」 —— 都会改变含义。

sections.text: 三种语域
Reporting 追求客观中立(「Officials announced…」)。Analysis 对数据进行解读(「What this means for…」)。Editorial / op-ed 则会表明立场(「It is high time we…」)。混用这三种语域是严重的语域错误。

rows: According to officials, the bill passed…
What this means for the wider economy…
It is high time we addressed…

sections.text: 引述句式

rows.source: according to sources familiar with the matter
rows.translation: 据熟悉此事的消息人士透露

rows.source: amid concerns that markets may overheat
rows.translation: 在市场可能过热的担忧之中

rows.source: officials say no decision has been made
rows.translation: 官员表示尚未做出决定

rows.source: the company declined to comment
rows.translation: 公司拒绝置评

rows.source: the spokesperson did not immediately respond
rows.translation: 发言人未立即回应

sections.text: 带有立场色彩的词汇

items: claimed:声称(引述中带有距离感)
purportedly:声称的、所谓的(带怀疑色彩)
ostensibly:表面上(真实意图可能并非如此)

sections.text: 标题语法
新闻标题中冠词通常被省略(「Senate Passes Budget」),用现在时表示过去事件(「Court Rules Against…」),使用冒号加引号的格式(「Minister: "This is a turning point"」),并以来源后缀结尾(「…: Report」)。
评论文章中常见的套路化表达:「It is high time we…」、「One could argue…」、「Make no mistake…」、「Far from being a panacea…」。这些句式是 op-ed 与评论文章的标志;若用于纯报道,则属于严重的语域错位。

exercises.prompt: 「It is high time we acted on this.」 的语气如何?
options: 强调紧迫性的个人主张
exercises.answer: 强调紧迫性的个人主张
exercises.explanation: 「it is high time + 过去式」 是评论文章的固定句式;中文「该是 / 早该……了」是对应。属于 op-ed 标志性套路。

exercises.prompt: One could ___ that the system is broken.
exercises.answer: argue

exercises.prompt: Op-ed 套路化表达 — 中文释义
「不要搞错:这是一个时代的终结。」

exercises.prompt: 在 op-ed 中最合适的开头是哪一句?
options: It is high time we confronted the issue.
The court issued its ruling at noon.
exercises.answer: It is high time we confronted the issue.

exercises.prompt: 出你听到的句子
exercises.spokenText: Far from being a panacea, the proposal raises more questions than it answers.

Far from a panacea, the proposal raises more questions than it answers.
Far from being a panacea, the proposals raises more questions than it answer.
Far from being a panaceas, the proposal raises more questions than it answers.
exercises.answer: Far from being a panacea, the proposal raises more questions than it answers.

exercises.prompt: I, for ___, find the argument unconvincing.
exercises.answer: one
exercises.hint: 我个人觉得这个论点没有说服力。

exercises.prompt: 下列哪一句是 op-ed 中使用 hedging(软化语气)的范例?
exercises.answer: It seems plausible to suggest…

exercises.prompt: 「因此我们的呼吁很明确:必须采取行动。」
exercises.answer: Our call is therefore clear action must be taken

exercises.prompt: Far from being a ___, the policy is a partial fix.
exercises.answer: panacea
exercises.hint: 这项政策远不是万灵药，只是一种局部补救。

exercises.prompt: 「It is high time」 这一结构使用哪种时态?
options: 一般过去时 —— 仿佛已经发生般的强调用法
exercises.answer: 一般过去时 —— 仿佛已经发生般的强调用法
exercises.explanation: C1 化石用法:「It is high time we acted / we left」 用过去式表达「现在应该(却没)做」的虚拟意味。中文 L1 易写成现在时,会被改错。

exercises.prompt: 「这并不只是一个简单的监管问题。」
exercises.answer: This is not merely a question of regulation

lessons.description: 从片段中推断语域与立场

exercises.prompt: 「It is high time the regulator stepped in.」 属于哪种语域?
exercises.answer: op-ed

exercises.prompt: 「According to two sources, the deal was signed at 2 a.m.」 属于哪种语域?
exercises.answer: reporting

exercises.prompt: The CEO ___ the allegations.
exercises.answer: denied

exercises.prompt: 片段 — 所属语域
「The minister allegedly accepted gifts」 的语气如何?
exercises.answer: İddia düzeyinde, mesafeli

exercises.prompt: 出你听到的句子
exercises.spokenText: We urge lawmakers, in the strongest possible terms, to reconsider.
options: We urge lawmakers, in the strongest possible terms, to reconsider.
We urge lawmaker, in the strongest possible terms, to reconsider.
We urges lawmakers, in the strongest possible terms, to reconsider.
We urge lawmakers, in the strongest possible term, to reconsider.
exercises.answer: We urge lawmakers, in the strongest possible terms, to reconsider.

exercises.prompt: The proposal is ___ a step forward, but far from sufficient.
exercises.answer: ostensibly
exercises.hint: 这项提议表面上是个进步，但远远不够。

exercises.prompt: 「Reportedly, the firm is in talks with regulators.」 的语气如何?
exercises.answer: İhtiyatlı, kesinleşmemiş

exercises.prompt: 「消息人士透露,尚未达成任何决定。」
exercises.answer: Sources indicate that no decision has yet been reached

exercises.prompt: The firm ___ to comment when contacted.
exercises.answer: declined

exercises.prompt: 「Make no mistake: this is a watershed moment.」 属于哪种语域?
exercises.answer: op-ed

lessons.title: 对话:在电台访谈中回应记者的提问
lessons.description: 关于某条新闻的访谈 — 受访者视角

exercises.prompt: 电台节目 — 关于一项法案的质询

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: You've been one of the most vocal critics of the bill. Give our listeners the headline — what's at stake here?

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: 访谈开场 — 用分裂句转移重音
options: Basically the bill is dumb and everyone should hate it.
What's at stake isn't the headline number but the precedent — once this mechanism is in statute, future governments will reach for it reflexively.
Idk the bill exists and we're against it I guess.
turns.answer: What's at stake isn't the headline number but the precedent — once this mechanism is in statute, future governments will reach for it reflexively.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Supporters argue the safeguards are robust. Are they wrong, in your view?

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: 正式让步状语 — 请填空
turns.after: the safeguards look robust on paper, the enforcement mechanism is funded for two years and reviewed by the very ministry it constrains.
turns.answer: While

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: That sounds like a charge of bad faith. Are you saying the drafters knew?

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: 作为受访者使用模糊语 — 避免下结论
options: I'd stop short of imputing motive — but I'd note that the structural weakness is too convenient to be accidental, and that's a question for the legislators to answer.
I have no idea, don't ask me.
turns.answer: I'd stop short of imputing motive — but I'd note that the structural weakness is too convenient to be accidental, and that's a question for the legislators to answer.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Let me push back. Polling shows the public broadly supports the bill. Doesn't that count for something?

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: 倒装强调 — 请补全助动词
turns.after: I dismiss the polling — but support softens markedly once respondents see the enforcement clause, which is rarely included in the surveys.
turns.answer: would

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: If you could rewrite one clause tonight, which would it be?

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: 请选择一个具体、便于媒体引用的回答
options: Just delete the whole thing tbh.
I'd hand the review function to an independent body with multi-year funding and the power to compel disclosure — without that, the rest is window-dressing.
Idk man, hard to say in a sound bite.
turns.answer: I'd hand the review function to an independent body with multi-year funding and the power to compel disclosure — without that, the rest is window-dressing.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: We're nearly out of time. Final thought for the audience?

turns.speaker: you
turns.text: Read the enforcement clause, not the press release. The press release will not be what governs your life.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Thank you for joining us. That was a sharper conversation than most of us were expecting tonight.

topics.title: C1 — 总复习
topics.description: 综合 C1 所有主题的复习

guide.intro: 本部分将 C1 阶段涵盖的商务、学术、社会、习语、语法和辩论等主题融为一体。每道练习都会触及多个主题。

sections.text: 检查清单

items: 我能在商务文件中保持一致的正式语域。
我能在学术写作中恰当地使用模糊语。
我能在社会议题讨论中选用具有细微差别的形容词。
我能识别常见习语以及容易混淆的「假朋友」。
我能熟练使用倒装与分裂句。
我能用话语标记词(granted、conversely、hence)衔接句子。

lessons.title: 综合 1 — 商务与学术
lessons.description: 正式语域测试

exercises.prompt: 「Pursuant to our discussion」 用中文怎么翻译?(C1 商务正式语)
options: 根据(承接)我们之前的讨论
exercises.answer: 根据(承接)我们之前的讨论
exercises.explanation: 「Pursuant to」 是 C1 商务正式语,= 「根据 / 依照」。中文 L1 易把它和 「after」 混淆,但 「pursuant to」 强调承接关系,不只是时间先后。

exercises.prompt: A growing ___ of evidence indicates climate sensitivity.
exercises.answer: body
exercises.hint: 越来越多的证据表明气候系统具有敏感性。

exercises.prompt: 「我们可能难以达到这个数字。」
exercises.answer: We may have difficulty meeting that figure

exercises.prompt: 下列哪一句最贴合学术语气?
options: The findings appear to support our hypothesis.
exercises.answer: The findings appear to support our hypothesis.

exercises.prompt: 出你听到的句子
exercises.spokenText: Notwithstanding the delay, the deliverables remain unchanged.
options: Notwithstanding the delay, the deliverables remain unchanged.
Not withstanding the delay, the deliverable remain unchanged.
Notwithstanding the delays, the deliverables remained unchanged.
Notwithstand the delay, the deliverables remain unchanged.

exercises.prompt: I'd like to push ___ on that timeline.

exercises.prompt: 除了「实现某个项目」之外,「realize」 还有什么含义?
exercises.answer: 意识到 / 察觉到
exercises.explanation: 中文 L1 假朋友陷阱:「realize」 在英语中最常用的意思是「意识到」(I realized my mistake),而中文学生通常只熟悉「实现」一义。注意区分 「realize that…」(意识到)vs 「realize a plan」(实现)。

exercises.prompt: 「本研究提出了一个新的理论框架。」
exercises.answer: This study proposes a novel theoretical framework

exercises.prompt: These results ___ a robust effect.
exercises.answer: demonstrate
exercises.hint: 这些结果显示出一种稳健的效应。

lessons.title: 对话:高级顾问客户会议
lessons.description: 综合场景 — 观点、语域与习语

exercises.prompt: 客户会议 — 关于整体重组的建议

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: We've read the deck. Cut to the chase — do you genuinely think a wholesale restructure is warranted, or is this consultant theatre?

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: 开场 — 用分裂句给出诚实的判断
options: Yeah it's basically theatre but you're paying us so we did it.
What the analysis points to isn't theatre — the cost-to-serve gap is structural, and incremental fixes will compound rather than close it.
Honestly the deck is whatever, look at the cover slide.
turns.answer: What the analysis points to isn't theatre — the cost-to-serve gap is structural, and incremental fixes will compound rather than close it.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.text: To build on that — the diagnostic is consistent across three independent data cuts, which gives us a level of conviction we don't always have at this stage.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: Conviction is one thing. The board will want to know what the downside looks like if we move and the macro turns.

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: 正式条件状语 — 请填空
turns.after: the macro deteriorate further, the restructure actually shortens your cash runway by six to eight months, so the move is risk-reducing, not risk-adding.
turns.answer: Should

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: And the people piece? We've burned the workforce twice in five years. Another round and morale won't recover.

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: 习语 + 语域 — 请选出合适的回答
options: Honestly people get over it, that's life.
It's a fair concern — and one we'd want to handle with extreme care; the literature on change fatigue is unambiguous, and we'd recommend front-loading transparency rather than drip-feeding bad news.
Just rip the band-aid off bro, they'll deal.
turns.answer: It's a fair concern — and one we'd want to handle with extreme care; the literature on change fatigue is unambiguous, and we'd recommend front-loading transparency rather than drip-feeding bad news.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.text: We've sequenced the communications plan so the operating model is settled before the headcount conversation — that's a hard-won lesson from comparable programmes.

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: 倒装强调 — 请补全助动词
turns.before: Only by settling the operating model first
turns.after: we credibly tell people what their roles will look like — and that, in our experience, is the single biggest determinant of retention.
turns.answer: can

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: Suppose I greenlight Phase 1 tomorrow. What's the first thing that's going to go wrong, and how do we get ahead of it?

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: 请选出一个习语化的 C1 收尾
options: Nothing will go wrong, trust me bro.
Idk we'll just figure it out when it happens lol.
Mid-level managers will read the org chart before the narrative lands — so we'd want a cascade briefing inside forty-eight hours, otherwise the grapevine writes the story for you.
turns.answer: Mid-level managers will read the org chart before the narrative lands — so we'd want a cascade briefing inside forty-eight hours, otherwise the grapevine writes the story for you.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: Useful. Send me a revised mobilisation plan by Wednesday and I'll take it to the board.

turns.speaker: you
turns.text: Will do. We'll route a draft past your CFO first so the numbers are unimpeachable before the board sees them.
